edition_note: Indexed from the extracted text of an ATAP PDF supplied as the 2013 SIAM edition (its pages carry the draft date January 30, 2018). The atlas source `trefethen19` is the 2019 Extended Edition, whose Chapters 1–28 have the same chapter, theorem and exercise numbering; the Extended Edition's added chapters are not indexed. Page numbers are those of this PDF and may be off by a few pages in the 2019 print. The book has 41 numbered theorems (no lemmas, corollaries or numbered definitions; Chapters 1, 2, 13, 14, 26 and 28 state no theorem). Unnumbered definitions from the prose are labelled `Def <chapter> (<name>)`. Exercises are indexed only when they state a named classical result (orthogonality, Bernstein polynomials, Fejér, Bernstein's inequality and theorem, de la Vallée Poussin, Chebyshev monic minimality, …).

items.label: Def 2 (Chebyshev points)
items.name: Chebyshev points
items.statement: For $n\ge1$ the $(n+1)$-point Chebyshev grid is $x_j=\cos(j\pi/n)$, $0\le j\le n$ (the extrema of $T_n$; real parts of the $2n$th roots of unity).
items.note: NLAlib uses Mathlib's `node` for its Chebyshev interpolant.

items.label: Def 2 (Chebyshev interpolant)
items.name: Chebyshev interpolant
items.statement: The Chebyshev interpolant $p_n\in\mathcal P_n$ of $f$ is the unique polynomial of degree at most $n$ agreeing with $f$ at the $n+1$ Chebyshev points.
items.note: Defined as Mathlib `Lagrange.interpolate` on `Polynomial.Chebyshev.node`; the name says 'Analytic' but the definition takes any `F : ℂ → ℂ`.

items.label: Ex 2.4
items.name: Chebyshev points of the first kind
items.statement: The first-kind (Gauss–Chebyshev) points are $x_j=\cos((j+\tfrac12)\pi/(n+1))$, $0\le j\le n$, the zeros of $T_{n+1}$.
items.note: Indexed as a named definition stated in an exercise.

items.label: Def 3 (Chebyshev polynomials)
items.name: Chebyshev polynomials
items.statement: $T_k(x)=\operatorname{Re} z^k=\cos(k\theta)$ for $x=\cos\theta=(z+z^{-1})/2$; they satisfy $T_{k+1}=2xT_k-T_{k-1}$, so $T_k$ has degree $k$ and leading coefficient $2^{k-1}$, and $|T_k|\le1$ on $[-1,1]$.

items.label: Thm 3.1
items.name: Chebyshev series
items.statement: A Lipschitz continuous $f$ on $[-1,1]$ has a unique absolutely and uniformly convergent expansion $f=\sum_k a_kT_k$, with $a_k=\tfrac2\pi\int_{-1}^1 f(x)T_k(x)(1-x^2)^{-1/2}dx$ for $k\ge1$ and $\tfrac1\pi$ in place of $\tfrac2\pi$ for $k=0$.
items.note: NLAlib proves pointwise convergence of the Chebyshev series only for $f$ bounded and holomorphic on an open Bernstein ellipse; the Lipschitz case, absolute/uniform convergence, uniqueness and the weighted-integral formula (3.12) are missing (atlas candidate `chebyshev-series-convergence`).

items.label: Def 3 (Chebyshev coefficients)
items.name: Chebyshev coefficients and series
items.statement: The Chebyshev coefficients $a_k$ of $f$ are given by the weighted integrals (3.12), equivalently the cosine coefficients of $f(\cos\theta)$ or the Laurent coefficients of $f((z+z^{-1})/2)$ on $|z|=1$.
items.note: The contour/Fourier definition exists (it only reads values on $[-1,1]$); the weighted-integral form, linearity, exactness on polynomials and $|a_k|\le2\|f\|$ (atlas candidate `chebyshev-coefficients-def`) are not stated.

items.label: Ex 3.6
items.name: Chebyshev series of sign(x) and |x| (Bernstein 1914)
items.statement: For $\operatorname{sign}(x)$: $a_k=0$ for even $k$ and $a_k=\tfrac4\pi\tfrac{(-1)^{(k-1)/2}}{k}$ for odd $k$; for $|x|$: $a_0=2/\pi$, $a_k=0$ for odd $k$, $a_k=\tfrac4\pi\tfrac{(-1)^{k/2}}{1-k^2}$ for even $k\ge2$.
items.note: Proposed candidate `chebyshev-series-abs-sign` (trefethen19.candidates.json). The extracted text reads $(-1)^{k-1}$ for the sign coefficients, which is constant for odd $k$; the correct factor is $(-1)^{(k-1)/2}$. Check the print before citing.

items.label: Ex 3.7
items.name: Orthogonality of Chebyshev polynomials
items.statement: $\int_{-1}^1 T_jT_k(1-x^2)^{-1/2}dx=0$ for $j\ne k$, $=\pi$ for $j=k=0$ and $\pi/2$ for $j=k\ge1$.

items.label: Ex 3.12
items.name: Extrema and roots of Chebyshev polynomials
items.statement: $T_n$ has the $n$ simple roots $\cos((2k+1)\pi/(2n))$ and attains $\pm1$ on $[-1,1]$ exactly at $\cos(k\pi/n)$, $0\le k\le n$.

items.label: Ex 3.15
items.name: Chebyshev series of e^{ax}
items.statement: $e^{ax}=2\sum_{k\ge0}{}' I_k(a)T_k(x)$ (first term halved), with $I_k$ the modified Bessel function of the first kind.
items.note: Proposed candidate `chebyshev-series-exp-bessel` (trefethen19.candidates.json). Mathlib has no modified Bessel functions $I_k$.

items.label: Def 4 (Chebyshev projection)
items.name: Chebyshev projection (truncation)
items.statement: The degree-$n$ Chebyshev projection of $f$ is $f_n=\sum_{k=0}^n a_kT_k$, the truncation of its Chebyshev series.
items.note: The truncation is defined from the contour coefficients; its basic API (projection property $p_n=p$ for $\deg p\le n$, linearity) is part of the candidate `chebyshev-coefficients-def`.

items.label: Thm 4.1
items.name: Aliasing of Chebyshev polynomials
items.statement: For $n\ge1$, on the $(n+1)$-point Chebyshev grid $T_k$ takes the same values as $T_m$ with $m=|(k+n-1)\bmod 2n-(n-1)|\in[0,n]$; equivalently $T_m,T_{2n\pm m},T_{4n\pm m},\dots$ agree on the grid.
items.note: Proved as a helper of `chebyshev-approx-analytic` with the fold `min(k mod 2n, 2n − k mod 2n)`, which equals the book's index; the atlas entry `chebyshev-aliasing` is still marked candidate and should record this.

items.label: Thm 4.2
items.name: Aliasing formula for Chebyshev coefficients
items.statement: For Lipschitz $f$ with coefficients $a_k$ and Chebyshev interpolant $p_n$ ($n\ge1$) with coefficients $c_k$: $c_0=a_0+a_{2n}+a_{4n}+\cdots$, $c_n=a_n+a_{3n}+\cdots$, and $c_k=a_k+\sum_{\ell\ge1}(a_{2\ell n+k}+a_{2\ell n-k})$ for $1\le k\le n-1$.
items.note: NLAlib has $p_n=\sum_k a_kT_{\mathrm{alias}(k)}$ pointwise for $f$ holomorphic and bounded on a Bernstein ellipse; the Lipschitz hypothesis and the coefficient identities (4.5)–(4.7) are missing (candidate `chebyshev-aliasing`).

items.label: Ex 4.1
items.name: Node polynomial for Chebyshev points
items.statement: The monic node polynomial of the $n+1$ Chebyshev points $\cos(j\pi/n)$ is $2^{-n}(T_{n+1}-T_{n-1})$.
items.note: Proposed candidate `chebyshev-barycentric-weights` (trefethen19.candidates.json). NLAlib has only the first-kind analogue `nodal_chebyshevZero` ($2^{1-q}T_q$).

items.label: Def 5 (Lagrange basis and node polynomial)
items.name: Lagrange polynomials, node polynomial
items.statement: For distinct nodes $x_0,\dots,x_n$, $\ell_j$ is the degree-$n$ polynomial with $\ell_j(x_k)=\delta_{jk}$, $\ell_j(x)=\prod_{k\ne j}(x-x_k)/(x_j-x_k)$, and $\ell(x)=\prod_k(x-x_k)$ is the node polynomial; $p=\sum_jf_j\ell_j$ interpolates.

items.label: Thm 5.1
items.name: Barycentric interpolation formula
items.statement: Off the nodes the interpolant is $p(x)=\sum_j\frac{\lambda_jf_j}{x-x_j}\big/\sum_j\frac{\lambda_j}{x-x_j}$ with weights $\lambda_j=1/\prod_{k\ne j}(x_j-x_k)$, and $p(x_j)=f_j$.
items.note: Mathlib's second barycentric form with `nodalWeight` = the book's $\lambda_j$.

items.label: Thm 5.2
items.name: Barycentric interpolation in Chebyshev points
items.statement: At the Chebyshev points the barycentric weights may be taken as $(-1)^j$, halved for $j=0$ and $j=n$: $p(x)=\sum_j{}'\frac{(-1)^jf_j}{x-x_j}\big/\sum_j{}'\frac{(-1)^j}{x-x_j}$.
items.note: Proposed candidate `chebyshev-barycentric-weights` (trefethen19.candidates.json).

items.label: Thm 6.1
items.name: Weierstrass approximation theorem
items.statement: Every continuous $f$ on $[-1,1]$ is uniformly approximable by polynomials to any accuracy $\varepsilon>0$.

items.label: Ex 6.4
items.name: Bernstein's proof (Bernstein polynomials)
items.statement: For $f\in C[0,1]$ the Bernstein polynomials $B_n(x)=\sum_k f(k/n)\binom nk x^k(1-x)^{n-k}$ converge uniformly to $f$.

items.label: Ex 6.6
items.name: Fejér's theorem for Chebyshev series
items.statement: For any $f\in C[-1,1]$ the Cesàro means $S_n$ of the partial sums of its Chebyshev series converge uniformly to $f$; (b) Hermite–Fejér interpolants in the zeros of $T_n$ also converge.
items.note: Proposed candidate `fejer-chebyshev-means` (trefethen19.candidates.json). Part (a) is the target; part (b) (Hermite–Fejér) is low value.

items.label: Def 7 (total variation)
items.name: Bounded variation
items.statement: The total variation of $f$ on $[-1,1]$ is the supremum over partitions of $\sum|f(x_{i+1})-f(x_i)|$ (equal to $\|f'\|_1$ for absolutely continuous $f$); $f$ has bounded variation if it is finite.

items.label: Thm 7.1
items.name: Chebyshev coefficients of differentiable functions
items.statement:
If $f,\dots,f^{(
u-1)}$ are absolutely continuous on $[-1,1]$ and $f^{(
u)}$ has total variation $V$, then $|a_k|\le rac{2V}{\pi k(k-1)\cdots(k-
u)}\le rac{2V}{\pi(k-
u)^{
u+1}}$ for $k\ge
u+1$.

items.label: Thm 7.2
items.name: Convergence for differentiable functions
items.statement:
Under Thm 7.1's hypotheses with $
u\ge1$ and $n>
u$: $\|f-f_n\|\le rac{2V}{\pi
u(n-
u)^
u}$ and $\|f-p_n\|\le rac{4V}{\pi
u(n-
u)^
u}$.
items.note: NLAlib's `jackson-lipschitz` gives an $O(L/n)$ bound for Lipschitz $f$ by a different (convolution) construction; it is not a case of this theorem.

items.label: Def 8 (Bernstein ellipse)
items.name: Bernstein ellipse
items.statement: For $\rho>1$, $E_\rho$ is the open region bounded by the image of $|z|=\rho$ under the Joukowski map $x=(z+z^{-1})/2$: an ellipse with foci $\pm1$ and semi-axis sum $\rho$.
items.note: Defined as the Joukowski image of the annulus $\rho^{-1}<|w|<\rho$, which is the book's region; the atlas definition entry `bernstein-ellipse-def` is still candidate because its extra characterisations (foci form, $|T_n|$ bound on $E_\rho$) are not stated.

items.label: Thm 8.1
items.name: Chebyshev coefficients of analytic functions
items.statement: If $f$ extends analytically to the open Bernstein ellipse $E_\rho$ with $|f|\le M$ there, then $|a_0|\le M$ and $|a_k|\le2M\rho^{-k}$ for $k\ge1$.

items.label: Thm 8.2
items.name: Convergence for analytic functions
items.statement: Under Thm 8.1's hypotheses, for every $n\ge0$: $\|f-f_n\|\le\frac{2M\rho^{-n}}{\rho-1}$ and $\|f-p_n\|\le\frac{4M\rho^{-n}}{\rho-1}$.

items.label: Thm 8.3
items.name: Converse of Theorem 8.2
items.statement: If some polynomials $q_n\in\mathcal P_n$ satisfy $\|f-q_n\|\le C\rho^{-n}$ for all $n$ ($\rho>1$), then $f$ continues analytically to the open Bernstein ellipse $E_\rho$.
items.note: Proposed candidate `bernstein-converse` (trefethen19.candidates.json).

items.label: Ex 8.6
items.name: Bernstein's inequality on the ellipse
items.statement: If $\deg p\le d$ then $\sup_{\overline{E_\rho}}|p|\le\rho^d\max_{[-1,1]}|p|$.
items.note: NLAlib has only the real-axis case ($|p(x)|\le M|T_d(x)|\le M\rho^d$ for real $|x|\ge1$ on the ellipse); the complex bound is the candidate `bernstein-walsh-ellipse`.

items.label: Ex 8.10
items.name: Polynomial approximation of 1/x (CG convergence)
items.statement: For $0<m<M$, $1/x$ is approximable on $[m,M]$ by degree-$n$ polynomials with geometric error, rate $(1+2/\sqrt\kappa)^{-n}$ in terms of the condition number $\kappa$.
items.note: NLAlib proves the explicit bound $\frac2m\big(\frac{\sqrt\kappa-1}{\sqrt\kappa+1}\big)^n$ with $\kappa=M/m$, which is a faster rate than the exercise's. As printed ('for any $\kappa<M/m$') the exercise is too strong for small $\kappa$; with $\kappa=M/m$ it follows from the NLAlib bound.

items.label: Ex 8.11
items.name: Bernstein's theorem
items.statement: Thm 8.3 remains true under the weaker hypothesis $\limsup_n\|f-q_n\|^{1/n}\le\rho^{-1}$.
items.note: Proposed candidate `bernstein-converse` (trefethen19.candidates.json).

items.label: Thm 9.1
items.name: Gibbs phenomenon for Chebyshev interpolants
items.statement: The Chebyshev interpolants of $\operatorname{sign}(x)$ have sup norms tending to $1.28228\ldots$ along odd $n$ and $1.06578\ldots$ along even $n$.
items.note: Asymptotic overshoot constants (not proved in the book); approximation of sign uses rates away from the jump (`sign-polynomial-approx`), not Gibbs constants.

items.label: Thm 9.2
items.name: Gibbs phenomenon for Chebyshev projections
items.statement: The Chebyshev projections of $\operatorname{sign}(x)$ have sup norms tending to $\tfrac2\pi\operatorname{Si}(\pi)=1.17898\ldots$.
items.note: Asymptotic overshoot constant; no consumer.

items.label: Def 10 (best approximation)
items.name: Best (minimax) approximation
items.statement: $p^*\in\mathcal P_n$ is a best approximation of $f\in C[-1,1]$ if it minimises $\|f-p\|_\infty$; its error is $E_n(f)$.
items.note: NLAlib has `isLeast_chebyshev_minimax` / `isLeast_chebyshev_monic_minimax` for specific problems but no general $E_n(f)$.

items.label: Def 10 (equioscillation)
items.name: Equioscillation, alternant
items.statement: $f-p$ equioscillates at $k$ points if there are $x_1<\dots<x_k$ in $[-1,1]$ with $f(x_j)-p(x_j)=\pm(-1)^j\|f-p\|$; $n+2$ such points form an alternant.

items.label: Thm 10.1
items.name: Equioscillation characterization of best approximants
items.statement: Each continuous $f$ on $[-1,1]$ has a unique best approximation $p^*\in\mathcal P_n$; for real $f$, $p^*$ is real and $p\in\mathcal P_n$ equals $p^*$ iff $f-p$ equioscillates at at least $n+2$ points.

items.label: Ex 10.3
items.name: de la Vallée Poussin lower bound
items.statement: If $f-p$ ($p\in\mathcal P_n$) alternates in sign at $n+2$ points with $|f-p|\ge\varepsilon$ there, then $\|f-p^*\|\ge\varepsilon$.

items.label: Ex 10.7
items.name: Bernstein's lethargy theorem
items.statement: For any sequence $\varepsilon_n\downarrow0$ there is $f\in C[-1,1]$ with $\|f-p_n^*\|\ge\varepsilon_n$ for all $n$.
items.note: Existence of arbitrarily slowly approximable functions; no consumer (lower bounds in RandNLA are for specific functions).

items.label: Ex 10.11
items.name: Chebyshev polynomials as best approximations
items.statement: The best degree-$n$ approximation to $x^{n+1}$ is $x^{n+1}-2^{-n}T_{n+1}$; equivalently $2^{-n}T_{n+1}$ is the monic polynomial of degree $n+1$ with the least sup norm $2^{-n}$ on $[-1,1]$.
items.note: This is where ATAP states monic minimality; atlas `chebyshev-monic-minimal` cites 'Thm 16.1', which is a different result.

items.label: Ex 10.12
items.name: Every best approximant is an interpolant
items.statement: The best approximation $p^*\in\mathcal P_n$ of a real $f\in C[-1,1]$ interpolates $f$ at some $n+1$ distinct points of $(-1,1)$.
items.note: Proposed candidate `best-approximant-interpolates` (trefethen19.candidates.json).

items.label: Ex 10.13
items.name: Marcinkiewicz's theorem
items.statement: For each fixed $f\in C[-1,1]$ there is a triangular array of nodes whose interpolants converge to $f$ (contrast with Faber's theorem).
items.note: Existence of $f$-dependent node arrays; no consumer.

items.label: Thm 11.1
items.name: Hermite interpolation formula
items.statement: For $f$ analytic in a region containing distinct nodes $x_0,\dots,x_n$ and a contour $\Gamma$ around them, $p(x)=\frac1{2\pi i}\int_\Gamma\frac{f(t)(\ell(t)-\ell(x))}{\ell(t)(t-x)}dt$ and, for $x$ inside $\Gamma$, $f(x)-p(x)=\frac1{2\pi i}\int_\Gamma\frac{\ell(x)f(t)}{\ell(t)(t-x)}dt$.
items.note: Proposed candidate `hermite-integral-formula` (trefethen19.candidates.json). The only interpolation-error formula ATAP states; the derivative (Cauchy) remainder of `interpolation-remainder` does not appear in the book.

items.label: Def 12 (potential and equilibrium measure)
items.name: Logarithmic potential, Chebyshev density
items.statement: Node sets define discrete potentials $u_n(s)=\sum_j\log|s-x_j|$; the continuum limit for $[-1,1]$ is the equilibrium (Chebyshev) measure $d\mu=\pi^{-1}(1-x^2)^{-1/2}dx$.
items.note: Potential-theoretic machinery with no NLA consumer.

items.label: Def 12 (uniformly distributed grids)
items.name: Uniformly distributed node sequences
items.statement: Grids are uniformly distributed on $[-1,1]$ if their node polynomials satisfy $\lim_n(\max_{[-1,1]}|\ell_n|)^{1/n}=\tfrac12$ (the capacity of the interval).
items.note: Potential theory; no consumer.

items.label: Thm 12.1
items.name: Interpolation in uniformly distributed points
items.statement: If $\rho$ is the parameter of the largest Bernstein ellipse to which $f$ continues analytically, interpolants in any uniformly distributed grids satisfy $\lim_n\|f-p_n\|^{1/n}=\rho^{-1}$.
items.note: Potential-theoretic asymptotics (proof by reference to Gaier); the explicit Chebyshev-grid rate is Thm 8.2, already proved.

items.label: Def 12 (maximal convergence)
items.name: Maximally convergent sequences
items.statement: Approximations $p_n\in\mathcal P_n$ are maximally convergent if $\limsup_n\|f-p_n\|^{1/n}=\rho^{-1}$, the smallest possible value (Ch. 16 restates this).
items.note: Asymptotic notion with no consumer; the quantitative lower bound is the candidate `bernstein-converse`.

items.label: Def 13 (Runge phenomenon)
items.name: Runge function and Runge region
items.statement: Equispaced interpolants of $1/(1+25x^2)$ diverge near the endpoints; convergence for equispaced nodes requires analyticity in a larger 'football' region determined by the equispaced potential.
items.note: Negative result about equispaced interpolation; quantified in the index by Thm 15.2 (15.9).

items.label: Def 15 (Lebesgue function and constant)
items.name: Lebesgue function and Lebesgue constant
items.statement: For nodes $x_0,\dots,x_n$, $\lambda(x)=\sum_j|\ell_j(x)|$ and $\Lambda=\sup_{[-1,1]}\lambda$, the $\infty$-norm of the interpolation operator; more generally $\Lambda=\|L\|$ for a linear projection $L:C[-1,1]\to\mathcal P_n$.

items.label: Thm 15.1
items.name: Near-best approximation and Lebesgue constants
items.statement: If $L$ is a linear projection of $C[-1,1]$ onto $\mathcal P_n$ with Lebesgue constant $\Lambda$, then $\|f-Lf\|\le(\Lambda+1)\|f-p^*\|$.
items.note: Proposed candidate `chebyshev-projection-lebesgue-constant` (trefethen19.candidates.json). The atlas candidate states it for interpolation only; the book's statement is for any linear projection (needed for Chebyshev truncation).

items.label: Thm 15.2
items.name: Lebesgue constants for polynomial interpolation
items.statement: For any $n+1$ distinct nodes in $[-1,1]$, $\Lambda_n\ge\frac2\pi\log(n+1)+0.52125\ldots$; for Chebyshev points $\Lambda_n\le\frac2\pi\log(n+1)+1$ and $\Lambda_n\sim\frac2\pi\log n$; for equispaced points $\Lambda_n>2^{n-2}/n^2$ ($n\ge1$) and $\Lambda_n\sim2^{n+1}/(en\log n)$.
items.note: Proposed candidate `lebesgue-constant-lower-bound` (trefethen19.candidates.json). Existing candidate covers (15.8a); the general lower bound (15.7) and the equispaced bound (15.9a) are the new candidate `lebesgue-constant-lower-bound`.

items.label: Thm 15.3
items.name: Lebesgue constants for Chebyshev projection
items.statement: For $n\ge1$ the Lebesgue constant of degree-$n$ Chebyshev truncation is $\Lambda_n=\frac1{2\pi}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}\left|\frac{\sin((n+1/2)t)}{\sin(t/2)}\right|dt$ (the Dirichlet-kernel $L^1$ norm), with $\Lambda_n\le\frac4{\pi^2}\log(n+1)+3$ and $\Lambda_n\sim\frac4{\pi^2}\log n$.
items.note: Proposed candidate `chebyshev-projection-lebesgue-constant` (trefethen19.candidates.json). The extracted text of (15.10) shows no absolute value (probably lost in extraction); the Lebesgue constant is the $L^1$ norm of the Dirichlet kernel.

items.label: Thm 16.1
items.name: Chebyshev projections and interpolants are near-best
items.statement: For $f\in C[-1,1]$ and $n\ge1$: $\|f-f_n\|\le(4+\frac4{\pi^2}\log(n+1))\|f-p_n^*\|$ and $\|f-p_n\|\le(2+\frac2\pi\log(n+1))\|f-p_n^*\|$.
items.note: Proposed candidate `chebyshev-projection-lebesgue-constant` (trefethen19.candidates.json). Interpolant half is in the conclusion of candidate `lebesgue-constant-chebyshev`; projection half is in the new `chebyshev-projection-lebesgue-constant`.

items.label: Def 17 (orthogonal polynomials)
items.name: Orthogonal polynomials and their three-term recurrence
items.statement: For a weight $w>0$ on $(-1,1)$ with $\int w<\infty$, $p_0,p_1,\dots$ ($\deg p_n=n$) are orthogonal for $(f,g)=\int wf\bar g$; they satisfy a three-term recurrence $p_{n+1}=(x-\alpha_n)p_n-\beta_np_{n-1}$ (17.8).
items.note: NLAlib has orthonormal polynomials and their three-term recurrence for the discrete spectral measure $\mu_b$ of a symmetric matrix (Lanczos); a general weight/measure is missing (see candidates `orthogonal-polynomial-zeros`, `gauss-quadrature-general-measure`). As printed, (17.8) uses the coefficients $(xp_n,p_k)$ for monic $p_k$; the correct coefficients are $(xp_n,p_k)/(p_k,p_k)$.

items.label: Def 17 (Legendre polynomials)
items.name: Legendre polynomials and points
items.statement: The orthogonal polynomials for $w\equiv1$, normalised by $P_n(1)=1$: $\int_{-1}^1P_jP_k=\frac{2}{2k+1}\delta_{jk}$ and $(k+1)P_{k+1}=(2k+1)xP_k-kP_{k-1}$; Legendre points are their zeros.
items.note: Mathlib has only the shifted Legendre polynomials on $[0,1]$ (definition, coefficients, degree, symmetry); orthogonality (17.5) and the recurrence (17.6) are not stated. No RandNLA consumer, so not proposed.

items.label: Ex 17.4
items.name: Zeros of orthogonal polynomials
items.statement: The zeros of each orthogonal polynomial $p_n$ for a weight on $[-1,1]$ are real, simple and lie in $(-1,1)$.
items.note: Proposed candidate `orthogonal-polynomial-zeros` (trefethen19.candidates.json).

items.label: Ex 17.8
items.name: Minimality of orthogonal polynomials
items.statement: Among monic polynomials $q$ of degree $n$, the monic orthogonal polynomial $p_n$ minimises $(q,q)$.
items.note: Proved for the discrete spectral measure $\mu_b$ ($\|p(A)b\|^2=\int p^2d\mu_b$, minimiser the characteristic polynomial of the Krylov compression, with uniqueness); the statement for a general weight is missing.

items.label: Def 18 (colleague matrix)
items.name: Colleague and comrade matrices
items.statement: The colleague matrix is the almost-tridiagonal matrix of Thm 18.1 built from Chebyshev coefficients; for other orthogonal-polynomial bases the analogue is the comrade matrix.
items.note: Proposed candidate `colleague-matrix` (trefethen19.candidates.json).

items.label: Thm 18.1
items.name: Polynomial roots and colleague matrix eigenvalues
items.statement: The roots of $p=\sum_{k=0}^na_kT_k$ ($a_n\ne0$) are the eigenvalues of the $n\times n$ colleague matrix: tridiagonal with entries $\tfrac12$ (first row $1$) plus a last-row correction $-a_k/(2a_n)$.
items.note: Proposed candidate `colleague-matrix` (trefethen19.candidates.json).

items.label: Def 19 (interpolatory quadrature)
items.name: Interpolatory, Clenshaw–Curtis and Gauss quadrature
items.statement: An $(n+1)$-point rule $I_n=\sum_kw_kf(x_k)$ is interpolatory if $w_k=\int_{-1}^1\ell_k$; Clenshaw–Curtis uses Chebyshev points, Gauss uses the zeros of $P_{n+1}$, Newton–Cotes equispaced points.
items.note: Proposed candidate `gauss-quadrature-general-measure` (trefethen19.candidates.json). NLAlib's Gauss rule exists only for the spectral measure (`lanczos-gauss-quadrature`).

items.label: Thm 19.1
items.name: Polynomial degree of quadrature formulas
items.statement: An $(n+1)$-point interpolatory rule is exact on $\mathcal P_n$; the $(n+1)$-point Gauss rule is exact on $\mathcal P_{2n+1}$.
items.note: Proposed candidate `gauss-quadrature-general-measure` (trefethen19.candidates.json). Gauss exactness to degree $2q-1$ is proved for the spectral measure $\mu_b$ (NLAlib) and for the Chebyshev weight (Mathlib, Gauss–Chebyshev); the Legendre-weight (Lebesgue measure) rule of the book and the interpolatory part are missing.

items.label: Thm 19.2
items.name: Integral of a Chebyshev series
items.statement: $\int_{-1}^1\sum_{k=0}^nc_kT_k(x)dx=\sum_{k\text{ even}}\frac{2c_k}{1-k^2}$; equivalently $\int_{-1}^1T_k=\frac2{1-k^2}$ for even $k$ and $0$ for odd $k$.
items.note: Proposed candidate `chebyshev-integral-formula` (trefethen19.candidates.json).

items.label: Thm 19.3
items.name: Quadrature formulas for analytic integrands
items.statement: If $f$ is analytic and bounded by $M$ in $E_\rho$, then $(n+1)$-point Clenshaw–Curtis ($n\ge2$) has $|I-I_n|\le\frac{64}{15}\frac{M\rho^{1-n}}{\rho^2-1}$ and $(n+1)$-point Gauss ($n\ge1$) has $|I-I_n|\le\frac{64}{15}\frac{M\rho^{-2n}}{\rho^2-1}$.
items.note: Proposed candidate `gauss-clenshaw-curtis-quadrature-error` (trefethen19.candidates.json). NLAlib's `lanczos-quadrature-analytic-error` is the Gauss analogue for a spectral measure with the weaker constant $4M\rho^{1-2q}/(\rho-1)$ per unit mass (a $q$-point rule), derived from Thm 8.2 and exactness; it is not this statement (different measure, different constant) and there is no Clenshaw–Curtis result.

items.label: Thm 19.4
items.name: Quadrature formulas for differentiable integrands
items.statement:
Clenshaw–Curtis and Gauss converge for every continuous $f$; if $f^{(
u)}$ ($
u\ge1$) has bounded variation $V$, Clenshaw–Curtis has $|I-I_n|\le rac{32}{15} rac{V}{\pi
u(n-
u)^
u}$ ($n>
u$) and Gauss $|I-I_n|\le rac{32}{15} rac{V}{\pi
u(n-2
u-1)^{2
u+1}}$ ($n>2
u+1$).
items.note: Proposed candidate `gauss-clenshaw-curtis-quadrature-error` (trefethen19.candidates.json). NLAlib's `lanczos-quadrature-lipschitz-error` is a related Gauss bound for Lipschitz $f$ and spectral measures ($\pi L(c-a)/(4q)$); not a case of this theorem.

items.label: Thm 19.5
items.name: Clenshaw–Curtis quadrature for differentiable integrands
items.statement:
Under Thm 19.4's hypotheses, Clenshaw–Curtis also satisfies the Gauss-type bound $ rac{32}{15} rac{V}{\pi
u(n-2
u-1)^{2
u+1}}$ for all sufficiently large $n$ (depending on $
u$ only).
items.note: Proposed candidate `gauss-clenshaw-curtis-quadrature-error` (trefethen19.candidates.json). Proof only by reference [Trefethen 2008]; priority later.

items.label: Thm 19.6
items.name: Barycentric weights for Legendre points
items.statement: With Gauss nodes $x_k$ and weights $w_k$, the numbers $\lambda_k=(-1)^k\sqrt{(1-x_k^2)w_k}$ are valid barycentric weights for interpolation in Legendre points.
items.note: Computational formula for Legendre barycentric weights; no consumer.

items.label: Def 20 (CF approximation)
items.name: Carathéodory–Fejér approximation
items.statement: The CF approximant of degree $n$ is built from the leading singular value and vector of a Hankel matrix of Chebyshev coefficients of $f$.
items.note: Near-best approximation algorithm via Hankel SVD; complex-analytic, no consumer.

items.label: Thm 20.1
items.name: Carathéodory–Fejér–Schur theorem
items.statement: The CF approximation problem on the unit circle has a unique solution $\tilde P$, with error $(G-\tilde P)(z)=\lambda z^{n+1}\overline{u(z)}/u(z)$ mapping the circle to a circle of radius $|\lambda|$ with winding number $\ge n+1$ ($=n+1$ if $|\lambda|$ is a simple top singular value).
items.note: Complex-analytic Hankel/CF theory; no consumer.

items.label: Thm 20.2
items.name: Accuracy of polynomial CF approximation
items.statement: For $f$ with Lipschitz $(3m+3)$rd derivative and $f^{(m+1)}(0)\ne0$, on $[-s,s]$ as $s\to0$: $\|f-p^*\|=\Theta(s^{m+1})$ while $\|p^{CF}-p^*\|=O(s^{3m+4})$.
items.note: CF asymptotics; no consumer.

items.label: Thm 21.1
items.name: Geometric convergence of derivatives
items.statement:
If $f$ continues analytically to the closed ellipse $\overline{E_ho}$, then for each $
u\ge0$, $\|f^{(
u)}-f_n^{(
u)}\|=O(ho^{-n})$ and $\|f^{(
u)}-p_n^{(
u)}\|=O(ho^{-n})$.
items.note: Derivative accuracy for spectral methods; no consumer (Markov's inequality, already proved, covers the polynomial side).

items.label: Def 21 (differentiation matrix)
items.name: Spectral differentiation matrix
items.statement: The $(n+1)\times(n+1)$ matrix mapping values of $p\in\mathcal P_n$ on a grid to values of $p'$ on the same grid.
items.note: Spectral collocation for ODEs; no RandNLA consumer.

items.label: Def 22 (transplanted approximation)
items.name: Conformally transplanted approximants
items.statement: Approximations $p(g^{-1}(x))$ for an analytic map $g:[-1,1]\to[-1,1]$ (e.g. 'sausage maps'), which are not polynomials in $x$.
items.note: Non-polynomial approximation spaces; no consumer.

items.label: Thm 22.1
items.name: Transformed Chebyshev series
items.statement: For $g$ analytic and increasing from $[-1,1]$ onto itself and Lipschitz $f$, $f(x)=\sum_ka_kT_k(g^{-1}(x))$ absolutely, with $a_k$ the Chebyshev coefficients of $f\circ g$.
items.note: Change of variables in Thm 3.1; non-polynomial approximants, no consumer.

items.label: Thm 22.2
items.name: Transformed coefficients of analytic functions
items.statement: If $g$ continues to $E_\rho$ and $f$ to $g(E_\rho)$ with $|f|\le M$ there, the transformed coefficients obey $|a_k|\le2M\rho^{-k}$ and the transformed truncations/interpolants have errors $\le2M\rho^{-n}/(\rho-1)$ and $4M\rho^{-n}/(\rho-1)$.
items.note: Thm 8.1–8.2 applied to $f\circ g$; non-polynomial approximants, no consumer. The extracted text of (22.4) reads $\rho^{-n}$ where $\rho^{-k}$ is meant.

items.label: Def 23 (rational functions of type (m,n))
items.name: Rational type, exact type
items.statement: $r$ is of type $(m,n)$, $r\in R_{mn}$, if $r=p/q$ with $\deg p\le m$, $\deg q\le n$; in lowest terms its exact type is $(\mu,\nu)$.
items.note: Proposed candidate `rational-equioscillation` (trefethen19.candidates.json). Needed only for the rational best-approximation candidate; priority later.

items.label: Thm 23.1
items.name: Partial fraction representation
items.statement: Each $r\in R_{mn}$ has a unique representation $r=p_0+\sum_kp_k((x-\xi_k)^{-1})$ with $p_0$ polynomial of degree $\le m$, $p_k(0)=0$, $\deg p_k=\nu_k\ge1$, $\sum\nu_k\le n$.
items.note: Mathlib states existence and uniqueness of partial fractions for products of powers of pairwise coprime monic factors (the book's case: linear factors $x-\xi_k$ over $\mathbb C$); the degree bookkeeping $\deg p_0\le m$, $\sum\nu_k\le n$ is immediate but not stated.

items.label: Def 24 (defect)
items.name: Defect of a rational function
items.statement: For $r\in R_{mn}$ of exact type $(\mu,\nu)$ the defect is $d=\min(m-\mu,n-\nu)$ (with $d=n$ for $r=0$).
items.note: Proposed candidate `rational-equioscillation` (trefethen19.candidates.json).

items.label: Thm 24.1
items.name: Equioscillation characterization of rational best approximants
items.statement: A real $f\in C[-1,1]$ has a unique best real approximation $r^*\in R_{mn}$, and real $r\in R_{mn}$ equals $r^*$ iff $f-r$ equioscillates at at least $m+n+2-d$ points, $d$ the defect of $r$.
items.note: Proposed candidate `rational-equioscillation` (trefethen19.candidates.json).

items.label: Def 24 (Walsh table)
items.name: Walsh table
items.statement: The array of best real rational approximants $r^*_{mn}$ of $f$ indexed by $m,n\ge0$.
items.note: rational-function theory (Walsh/Padé structure) with no consumer in randomized NLA

items.label: Thm 24.2
items.name: Square blocks in the Walsh table
items.statement: The Walsh table of a real $f\in C[-1,1]$ splits into exactly square blocks of identical entries (one infinite if $f$ is rational), except that an entry $r=0$ fills all columns left of some index.
items.note: rational-function theory (Walsh/Padé structure) with no consumer in randomized NLA

items.label: Ex 24.5
items.name: de la Vallée Poussin lower bound (rational)
items.statement: If $f-r$ ($r\in R_{mn}$ real, defect $d$) alternates in sign at $m+n+2-d$ points with $|f-r|\ge\varepsilon$ there, then $\|f-r^*\|\ge\varepsilon$.
items.note: Proposed candidate `rational-equioscillation` (trefethen19.candidates.json).

items.label: Thm 25.1
items.name: Approximation of |x| on [−1,1]
items.statement: The best errors satisfy $E_{n,0}(|x|)\sim\beta/n$ with $\beta=0.2801\ldots$ (Bernstein's constant; Varga–Carpenter) and $E_{n,n}(|x|)\sim8e^{-\pi\sqrt n}$ (Stahl).
items.note: Proposed candidate `abs-best-approx-asymptotics` (trefethen19.candidates.json). Assume only; deep asymptotics.

items.label: Thm 25.2
items.name: Approximation of e^x on (−∞,0]
items.statement: Best type-$(0,n)$ rational approximations of $e^x$ on $(-\infty,0]$ satisfy $\lim_nE_{0n}^{1/n}=1/3$ (Schönhage), and type $(n,n)$ satisfy $E_{nn}\sim2H^{n+1/2}$, $H=1/9.2890\ldots$ (Halphen's constant; Aptekarev).
items.note: Proposed candidate `exp-rational-halfline` (trefethen19.candidates.json). Assume only; deep asymptotics.

items.label: Def 26 (rational interpolation)
items.name: Cauchy (rational) interpolation problem
items.statement: Find $r\in R_{mn}$ with $r(x_j)=f_j$ at $m+n+1$ points; solutions need not exist (unattainable points), and the linearized form $p(x_j)=f_jq(x_j)$ is solved via an SVD.
items.note: rational-function theory (Walsh/Padé structure) with no consumer in randomized NLA

items.label: Def 27 (Padé approximant)
items.name: Padé approximant
items.statement: The type-$(m,n)$ Padé approximant $r_{mn}$ of a Taylor series $f$ is the $r\in R_{mn}$ making $(f-r)(z)=O(z^{k})$ with $k$ maximal.
items.note: rational-function theory (Walsh/Padé structure) with no consumer in randomized NLA

items.label: Thm 27.1
items.name: Characterization of Padé approximants
items.statement: For each $m,n\ge0$, $f$ has a unique Padé approximant $r_{mn}\in R_{mn}$, and $r\in R_{mn}$ equals it iff $(f-r)(z)=O(z^{m+n+1-d})$, $d$ the defect of $r$.
items.note: rational-function theory (Walsh/Padé structure) with no consumer in randomized NLA

items.label: Thm 27.2
items.name: Square blocks in the Padé table
items.statement: The Padé table of any $f$ splits into exactly square blocks of identical entries, with the same exception for $r=0$ as Thm 24.2.
items.note: rational-function theory (Walsh/Padé structure) with no consumer in randomized NLA

items.label: Thm 27.3
items.name: Linear algebra solution of Padé problem
items.statement: Any nonzero null vector $b$ of the Toeplitz matrix $C$ of (27.8), with $a$ from (27.6), gives $p/q=r_{mn}$, the unique Padé approximant.
items.note: rational-function theory (Walsh/Padé structure) with no consumer in randomized NLA

items.label: Thm 27.4
items.name: Structure of a Padé approximant
items.statement: If $r_{mn}=\hat p/\hat q$ has exact type $(\mu,\nu)$, defect $d$, deficiency $\lambda$ and $\chi=d-\lambda$, then $C$ has rank $n-\chi$ and $(p,q)$ solve (27.5) iff $p=\pi\hat p$, $q=\pi\hat q$ for some $\pi\in\mathcal P_d$ divisible by $z^\lambda$.
items.note: rational-function theory (Walsh/Padé structure) with no consumer in randomized NLA

items.label: Def 28 (convergence acceleration)
items.name: Richardson, Aitken Δ², Shanks/epsilon extrapolation
items.statement: Sequence-acceleration methods obtained from polynomial (Richardson) or Padé-type rational (Aitken $\Delta^2$, Shanks, epsilon, eta) extrapolation of partial sums.
items.note: Extrapolation algorithms with no theorem stated and no consumer.
